summary: Reviewed the final state of app/label_stub.py, app/label_pipeline.py, tests/test_label_stub.py and tests/test_label_pipeline_source_review.py at the T0009 head, against the prior review result (.ai/handoffs/T0009-2.result.json) as the baseline, because Bash/git is disabled in this session so the literal 57a6c73..ec48fa8 patch text could not be read. All seven prior findings are closed in code and covered by regressions: the adaptive all-statement fitter is now selected on orientation-independent shipped_safety_layout (label_stub.py:1532-1535, 1599-1644) instead of the former width>height gate, with a portrait dense regression that calls assert_safety_transport_footer_clearance (tests/test_label_stub.py:907-944); the standard/portrait DOT branch now consumes identification_number_font_size in a 180x70 pt box (label_stub.py:263-268, 1683-1691) and the portrait test asserts font-size=48 (tests/test_label_stub.py:943); the compact DOT flags are emitted inside the translate(215, y_offset+35) detail group at group-local x with width bounds (label_stub.py:237-238, 1692-1704) and the test asserts their y equals the hazard-class and packing-group row y (tests/test_label_stub.py:1400-1404); both DOT branches print a visible "REFERENCE ONLY - APPLY SEPARATE DOT LABEL" caption plus data-dot-role="reference" (label_stub.py:242-247, 305-314, test 1407-1434); the sample renderer lays out every approved pictogram in adaptive rows with no slice (label_stub.py:1386-1415, test 162-177); the fit failure is a typed LabelContentDoesNotFitError translated to a 400 LABEL_CONTENT_DOES_NOT_FIT with remediation (label_stub.py:23-24, 1123-1125, label_pipeline.py:1405-1411, test 422-441); and the NFPA footer prints the visible "NFPA 704 - SUPPLEMENTAL" heading with data-nfpa-role (label_stub.py:359-364, tests 760, 880). Required source-backed content is preserved: the shipped path formats every H and P statement without ellipsis (_format_all_statements, label_stub.py:950-981), optional product_uses is the only content dropped before the typed failure (label_stub.py:1626-1636), and only approved GHS/DOT assets can render (_format_pictograms label_stub.py:1195-1204, _format_dot_labels 1236-1242). No duplicate statement block is emitted in shipped mode because the legacy hazard/precautionary sections stay gated on not safety_columns (template lines 172, 194). Remaining items are four low geometry margins plus one unresolved prior low; no critical, high, or medium defect found.

findings.defect: The portrait/compact height budget reserves height-110 for the safety plus transport stack, but the template consumes 18 pt of inter-block gaps after the budgeted content (safety_block_height + 8 at line 168, dot_panel_height + 10 at line 319) while the footer rule sits at height-94. At saturation (block_height exactly equal to available_safety_height) the DOT panel bottom lands at height-92, i.e. 2 pt past the footer rule, and up to 10 pt short of the 8 pt clearance that assert_safety_transport_footer_clearance (tests/test_label_stub.py:39) requires.
findings.reasoning: Only the decorative footer rule is crossed (supplier text starts at height-77), so no required content is obscured, but a denser SDS that saturates the fitter would both print a DOT border over the footer rule and fail the project's own clearance regression. Minimal fix: change the 110 in label_stub.py:1614 to 128, or subtract the two template gaps explicitly when computing available_safety_height.

findings.defect: line_width is clamped to a minimum of 18 characters regardless of the column geometry, so in the newly reachable narrow-portrait case the wrapped text can be wider than its column. For width=612 at 7 total columns (6 precaution columns) column_width=81.7 pt and continuation_indent=14 pt, while the computed line_width is 14 and is forced to 18: 18 chars at font 7.2 estimate 72.6 pt, so continuation lines reach 86.6 pt and cross ~5 pt into the next column. The same clamp forces first_line_width to its max(8, ...) floor, so a 14-character combined code such as P305+P351+P338 plus 8 text characters is ~97 pt wide in a 95.3 pt column at 6 columns. The candidate is still marked "fits" because only block_height is checked against available_height (line 1116).
findings.reasoning: The fitter can silently accept a horizontally overlapping layout for required H/P text, which is exactly the overlap class the task set out to prevent; the trigger is narrow (portrait plus enough statements to need 6-7 columns, which the reviewed CE SilaCure data does not reach at 3 columns), so impact is limited today but grows with denser SDS inputs. Minimal fix: when the computed line_width falls below the 18 floor, treat the candidate as not fitting (continue to the next font/column candidate) instead of clamping, or add a horizontal check that line_width * font_size * 0.56 + continuation_indent <= column_width - 8 to the fits condition.

findings.defect: In the compact (landscape) DOT branch the new reference caption baseline is y_offset+32 at font-size 6.5, while the purple header band occupies y_offset+5 to y_offset+28 (rect height 23 at line 221) across the same x range. Cap height at 6.5 pt is ~4.7 pt, so the top ~0.7 pt of every capital is drawn in brand_purple on the purple band fill and disappears.
findings.reasoning: The caption is the control that stops the 96 pt product-label diamond being read as the exterior DOT label, so degrading its top edge weakens the very marking just added; ~85 percent of each glyph is still on white, so it remains readable. Minimal fix: move the caption baseline to y_offset+34 (the image already starts at y_offset+34, which is below the baseline) or reduce the band height by 2 pt.

findings.defect: In the sample 4x6 six-pictogram branch the sixth icon is placed at x = 194 + 5*38 = 384 with width 34, reaching x=418, while the GHS band rect spans x=18 to x=414 (label_stub.py:1450, width-36). The icon crosses the panel border by ~4 pt. In the 7-to-9 icon branch the icons drop to 28 pt (about 9.9 mm) and the second row occupies y=141..169 against a band that ends at y=170, leaving ~1 pt of clearance.
findings.reasoning: No pictogram is dropped or clipped off-page, and the sample artifact carries the "verify SDS/TDS before production shipment" disclaimer, so this is a visual-quality defect rather than content loss; the 1 pt band clearance also leaves no margin for any future band or spacing change. Minimal fix: reduce sample_pictogram_spacing to 36 (or start_x to 190) in the <=6 branch and raise the band height, or derive start_x from the band right edge instead of a literal.

findings.defect: Prior review finding 7 is still open: in the non-dense shipped layout the signal word baseline is y_offset+21 at font-size 18 (signal_word_y_offset=21, signal_word_font_size=18) while the first pictogram cell starts at y_offset+22 at the same x=20, so an 18 pt descender (the g in Danger) intrudes about 3 pt into the first pictogram box.
findings.reasoning: Minor legibility degradation of required OSHA signal-word content in the layout this task is improving; it was classified low before and the delta did not change it, so it is carried, not introduced. Minimal fix: raise pictogram_y_offset to 26 (or lower signal_word_y_offset to 17) for the non-dense shipped case.

evidence_used: Read app/label_stub.py lines 1-1931 in full: SVG template compact DOT branch (216-249), standard DOT branch (250-317), footer and NFPA supplemental panel (343-382), _build_compact_safety_layout (1038-1126), _fit_safety_statements_for_page (1128-1193), _transport_detail_layout (1272-1310), sample 4x6 renderer (1340-1459), generate_svg layout computation (1461-1841).

app/label_stub.py:1532-1543: shipped_safety_layout and dense_safety_layout no longer depend on orientation; compact_compliance_layout (1527-1531) now only drives the compact DOT panel, confirming the portrait fitter gate is removed.

app/label_stub.py:1683-1691 and template 267-268: identification_number_font_size is 48 for <=6-character marks and is consumed by the standard (portrait) branch inside the 180x70 pt box at template 263.

Choose a larger label size or horizontal orientation."); Grep shows generate_svg has exactly one call site (app/label_pipeline.py:1390), and the apply_corrections path (1371-1384) raises before metadata.update, so no partial state is written.

tests/test_label_stub.py:21-39 (assert_safety_transport_footer_clearance), 162-177 (all nine sample pictograms), 713-760 and 880 (visible NFPA 704 - SUPPLEMENTAL plus data-nfpa-role), 822-883 (64 pt pictograms, 48 pt identification number, 96 pt reference diamond), 907-944 (portrait dense label keeps all 4 H and 18 P codes, 48 pt mark, footer clearance), 996-1029 (malformed multi-ID mark is fitted below 48 without ellipsis), 1360-1404 (compact flag width bound and row alignment), 1407-1434 (reference marking in both orientations).

.ai/handoffs/T0009-2.result.json: the seven prior findings used as the correction checklist.

Reused without rerun, as instructed: release.sh --verify-only pass at ec48fa8 (240 tests, browser E2E, 86 percent coverage, Railway-parity startup), the 93-test focused renderer/pipeline/validator run, the source-exact 12x9 and 9x12 inch PDFs retaining Danger, GHS05/GHS07, 4 H and 15 P statements, UN2735, proper shipping name, Class 8, PG III, responsible party, emergency phone and NFPA 3-1-0, the 48 pt mark measurement, the 64x64 pt pictograms, and the two 135 mm Class 8 stickers on the separate US Letter landscape sheet.
could_not_verify: The literal patch text of 57a6c73..ec48fa8. Bash, including git read commands, is disabled in this session, so I reviewed the final worktree state of the four named files and used the prior review result as the description of the pre-delta state. I therefore cannot attribute every line to this range; the four low findings above may be pre-existing margins rather than newly introduced.

Rendered-artifact confirmation of the geometry in the findings. I did not execute the renderer, so the 2 pt footer overshoot, the ~5 pt column overflow, the 0.7 pt caption overlap and the 4 pt sample-pictogram overhang are derived arithmetically from the template offsets and _estimated_text_width_units, not measured.

Font substitution in the deployed image. The 48 pt UN2735 mark fits the 180 pt box only with Arial or a metric-compatible face (~176 pt); a DejaVu Sans Bold substitution would be ~211 pt, overflowing the box and reaching the detail group at x=215. The reused evidence measured PDFs produced locally and a local Railway-parity startup, not a PDF rendered inside the deployed container, so the available font set there is unverified.

Whether the statement font floor used by the fitter in portrait for much denser SDS inputs (6.0 pt / 6.6 pt line height, label_stub.py:1048-1052) stays legible at actual size; the visual evidence covers the CE SilaCure data, which resolves to a larger font.

Any regulatory or legal determination. This review uses only the thresholds written into .ai/tasks/T0009.md (12 mm identification number, 100 mm minimum DOT label, 25.4 mm supplemental NFPA symbol) and makes no compliance certification.

Workplace-mode labels are unchanged and still truncate H/P statements through _format_statements (label_stub.py:899-920) via the non-shipped branch of _fit_safety_statements_for_page (1155-1193); the sample 4x6 artifact still carries no H/P statements. Both predate this delta and sit outside the stated correction scope, so I did not assess them as findings.
recommendation: Accept the correction delta: every prior critical, high and medium finding is closed in code with a matching regression, and required source-backed GHS and DOT content is preserved on both orientations with no detected content loss. Before any production deployment (which remains a human gate), fold in the two cheapest margins: raise the 110 pt reserve in app/label_stub.py:1614 so the saturated DOT panel cannot cross the footer rule, and move the compact reference caption baseline to y_offset+34 so its glyph tops leave the purple band. Treat the line_width max(18, ...) clamp as a fits-check condition rather than a clamp when next touching the fitter, and confirm an Arial-metric font is installed in the deployed image before relying on the 48 pt mark fitting its 180 pt box.
